title: The denominator is uses
hook: A €12 reusable item spreads its modeled purchase cost over repeated uses.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Find a reuse cost-per-use crossover under explicitly limited costs.

misconception: A reusable purchase is automatically cheaper at every use count.
objective: Find a reuse cost-per-use crossover under explicitly limited costs.

claims.text: A reusable item costs €12 once. Equivalent single-use items cost €0.20 each. Ongoing costs are excluded. Scaled model; fictional prices; upkeep excluded; equivalent service.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Uses=10, A=1.2€/use and B=0.2€/use. The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/",12,"x"]; B=0.2; x denotes Uses. At x=10, A=1.2, B=0.2; recall at x=25: B=0.2. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: Divide a one-time amount by uses to obtain its modeled cost per use. Here it matches €0.20 at sixty uses. This omits upkeep, lifespan and environmental impacts and makes no purchasing recommendation.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/",12,"x"]; B=0.2; x denotes Uses. At x=10, A=1.2, B=0.2; recall at x=25: B=0.2. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: A reusable item costs €12 once. Equivalent single-use items cost €0.20 each. Ongoing costs are excluded. Change only Uses to 25. What is B (Single-use) now? Correct: 0.2€/use. Use B's stated rule with Uses=25: it gives 0.2€/use. Divide a one-time amount by uses to obtain its modeled cost per use. Here it matches €0.20 at sixty uses. This omits upkeep, lifespan and environmental impacts and makes no purchasing recommendation.

recall.question: A reusable item costs €12 once. Equivalent single-use items cost €0.20 each. Ongoing costs are excluded. Change only Uses to 25. What is B (Single-use) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Uses=25: it gives 0.2€/use. Divide a one-time amount by uses to obtain its modeled cost per use. Here it matches €0.20 at sixty uses. This omits upkeep, lifespan and environmental impacts and makes no purchasing recommendation.

safety.assumptions: A reusable item costs €12 once. Equivalent single-use items cost €0.20 each. Ongoing costs are excluded.
safety.excluded: No chemical mixtures, medical advice, wiring, safety-device bypass, actual tariffs, financial recommendations, temperature, food-storage or food-safety instructions. All energy powers, durations and tariffs are illustrative.
